main_text.p: Sicut ambulauit feruus meus.) Interpretatio signi, atq; manifestum mandatum, denuncians intra trium annorum spatium, aut ut Hieronymus uidetur innuere, per totum triennium, Aegyptum atq; Aethiopiâ à rege Assyriorū grauiter affligendas. Estq; sententia: Sicut seruus meus Iesaias ambulauit nudus et discalceatus tribus annis, nō sine dedecore atq; ignominia: ita Aegyptij et Aethiopes post triennium à rege Assur gravissimè affligetur, necnō quamplurimi eorū nudi ac discalceati, omniq; contumeliarū genere adfecti in captiuitate abducetur. Tres anni vocantur signū & prodigiū super Aegyptū atq; Aethiopiā, quandoquidē destinati sunt pro certo tempore, quo adfligi ipsi debent. Captiuitas & transmigratio[?] pro captiuis atq; alio comigrare coactis. Pueros et senes posuit pro omnium ordinū hominibus. Nudū et discalceatū, discoopertos natibus, id est, omni generi miseriarū et cotumeliarū obnoxios: signū pro re signata per metonymiā. Neq; posset ulli maiore affici cotumelia, quàm si ad probrum nudi, præsertim nates et lubos, deducatur. 2.Samuel.10, Ammonitæ tali iniuria affecerunt legatos Dauidis. Cū dicit, In ignominiâ Aegypti: intellige pariter Aethiopiæ.

page.notes: Running head is "ANNOTATIONES." and page number 207 (printed "zo7"). Catchword "est:" is at the foot right, below the last line. Italic and roman boundaries in the commentary paragraph are approximate. The word after "Captiuitas &" is hard to read because of a line-end break; "transmigratio" is a best reading. Where the ligature "Ioan." and "Samuel" references are unclear, they are copied as printed. The text in the first paragraph is italic, and "tantùm" keeps its grave accent.
